title: Scatter Plots, Correlation and Residuals
seo_title: Algebra 1 Correlation Worksheets: Scatter Plots, Correlation Coefficient, Residuals and Causation (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 1 worksheets on scatter plots and correlation (S-ID.B.6, S-ID.C.7–9): describe correlation, interpret the correlation coefficient r, use and interpret lines of best fit, calculate residuals and tell correlation from causation. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: r is between −1 and 1: the sign is the direction, the size is the strength.
key_sub: Residual = actual − predicted. Correlation does not prove causation.
body_html:
How it works

A scatter plot shows the relationship between two variables. If the points rise, the correlation is positive; if they fall, it is negative. The closer they are to a straight line, the stronger it is.

The correlation coefficient r is between −1 and 1. Its sign gives the direction and its size gives the strength: |r| near 1 is strong, near 0 is weak.

A residual = actual − predicted. Residuals scattered randomly around 0 mean a line is a good model. Correlation does not mean causation: a third variable may affect both.

Example

A line of best fit is ŷ = 3x + 10. Find the residual for (4, 25).

Predicted: 3 × 4 + 10 = 22.

25 − 22.

Answer: 3

Example

r = −0.85. Describe the correlation.

Negative sign: one goes down as the other goes up.

0.85 is close to 1.

Answer: Strong negative

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a negative r means a weak relationship. −0.9 is strong.
  • Finding the residual as predicted − actual. It is actual − predicted.
  • Reading the slope as the starting value. The slope is the change per unit of x.
  • Assuming that correlation proves one variable causes the other.

faq.q: What does the correlation coefficient tell you?
faq.a: r measures the direction and strength of a linear relationship. It is between −1 and 1; values near ±1 are strong and values near 0 are weak.

faq.q: How do you calculate a residual?
faq.a: Subtract the predicted value from the actual value: residual = actual y − predicted y.

faq.q: What does a good residual plot look like?
faq.a: Points scattered randomly above and below zero with no pattern. A curve in the residuals means a line is not a good model.
Two variables can move together because of a third variable or by chance. Only a controlled experiment can show cause and effect.

items.q: A line of best fit for number of ads (x) and weekly sales in dollars (y) is y = 12x + 150. Predict the weekly sales in dollars when x = 4.
A line of best fit for number of ads (x) and weekly sales in dollars (y) is y = 12x + 150. What does the y-intercept mean?
c: The predicted weekly sales in dollars when number of ads is 0 is 150
The largest possible weekly sales in dollars is 150
The weekly sales in dollars goes up by 150 each time
The predicted weekly sales in dollars when number of ads is 0 is 12
items.e: The y-intercept is the predicted value of y when x = 0: 150.

items.q: A line of best fit for hours studied (x) and test score (y) is y = 2.5x + 40. What does the slope mean?
c: For each extra hour, the test score increases by about 2.5 points
For each extra hour, the test score decreases by about 2.5 points
For each extra hour, the test score changes by about 40 points
items.e: The slope is the change in y for each 1 unit increase in x: for each extra hour, the test score increases by about 2.5 points.

items.q: The line of best fit is ŷ = 4x + 17. A data point is (6, 45). What is its residual?
items.e: Predicted ŷ = 4 × 6 + 17 = 41. Residual = actual − predicted = 45 − 41 = 4.

items.q: The line of best fit is ŷ = 3x + 14. A data point is (8, 34). What is its residual?
items.e: Predicted ŷ = 3 × 8 + 14 = 38. Residual = actual − predicted = 34 − 38 = −4.

items.q: The line of best fit is ŷ = 2.5x + 21. A data point is (7, 37.5). What is its residual?
items.e: Predicted ŷ = 2.5 × 7 + 21 = 38.5. Residual = actual − predicted = 37.5 − 38.5 = −1.

items.q: The line of best fit is ŷ = 1.5x + 21. A data point is (3, 21.5). What is its residual?
items.e: Predicted ŷ = 1.5 × 3 + 21 = 25.5. Residual = actual − predicted = 21.5 − 25.5 = −4.

items.q: The line of best fit is ŷ = 1.5x + 8. A data point is (3, 11.5). What is its residual?
items.e: Predicted ŷ = 1.5 × 3 + 8 = 12.5. Residual = actual − predicted = 11.5 − 12.5 = −1.

items.q: A residual plot shows points scattered randomly above and below zero with no pattern. What does this suggest?
c: A linear model is a good fit
A linear model is a poor fit
items.e: Random residuals mean the line captures the pattern: a linear model fits well.

items.q: A data point has a negative residual. Where is it compared with the line of best fit?
c: To the left of the line
items.e: Residual = actual − predicted. Negative means the actual value is smaller: below the line.

items.q: The line of best fit is ŷ = 2x + 6. A data point is (3, 14). What is its residual?

items.q: A residual plot shows a clear U-shaped pattern. What does this suggest?
c: The correlation is strong and linear
A linear model is a good fit
A linear model is not a good fit; the data is curved
items.e: A pattern in the residuals means the line misses the shape of the data: a curve would fit better.

items.e: Predicted ŷ = 2.5 × 3 + 22 = 29.5. Residual = actual − predicted = 31.5 − 29.5 = 2.

items.q: Ice cream sales and drowning incidents have a strong positive correlation. Which conclusion is best?
c: The correlation must be a mistake
Both probably rise in hot weather; ice cream does not cause drowning
items.e: A third variable (hot weather) affects both. Correlation does not prove causation.

items.q: Which situation is most likely to show causation, not just correlation?
c: The more hours a heater runs, the more electricity is used
Students with bigger feet read better
Towns with more churches have more crime
People who own boats live longer
items.e: Running a heater directly uses electricity: a cause. The others are linked by other variables, such as age or population.

items.q: A line of best fit for children aged 2–10 predicts height from age. Should it be used to predict the height of a 40-year-old?
c: No, 40 is far outside the data (extrapolation)
No, because the slope is positive
Yes, if the correlation is strong
Yes, the line works for all ages
items.e: Predicting far outside the data range is risky: people stop growing. No.

items.q: What is interpolation?
c: Predicting beyond the range of the data
Predicting within the range of the data
items.e: Interpolation predicts inside the data's range; extrapolation goes outside it.

items.q: The correlation between two variables is −0.92. Which statement is true?
c: As one increases, the other tends to decrease, and the relationship is strong
The relationship is weak because r is negative
items.e: The sign shows direction (negative) and |−0.92| is close to 1: strong and negative.

items.q: Which value of r is impossible?
items.e: r is always between −1 and 1, so 1.3 is impossible.

items.q: A residual is +6. What does it mean?
c: The actual value is 6 more than the line predicted
The point is 6 units to the right
The line predicted 6 more than the actual value
items.e: Residual = actual − predicted = +6: the actual value is 6 above the prediction.

items.q: Two lines are fitted to the same data. Line A's residuals are mostly between −1 and 1; line B's are between −5 and 5. Which fits better?
items.e: Smaller residuals mean the predictions are closer to the data: line A.

items.q: A study finds that students who eat breakfast get higher grades. What is the best conclusion?
c: Higher grades cause students to eat breakfast
There is an association, but other factors may explain it
items.e: An observational study shows association, not cause. Home routines, sleep and other factors may be involved.

items.q: A scatter plot's points rise steeply and lie almost exactly on a line. Which value of r fits best?
items.e: Rising and very close to a line: r ≈ 0.98.

items.q: If r = 0, which statement is true?
c: There is no relationship of any kind
All points are on a horizontal line
items.e: r measures linear relationships only. A curved pattern can still give r ≈ 0.

items.q: The equation ŷ = 15x + 200 predicts monthly sales ŷ from advertising dollars x (in hundreds). If $400 is spent on ads, what are the predicted sales?
A line of best fit has slope 0. What does that suggest?
items.e: A flat line predicts the same y for every x: x does not help predict y.

items.q: Which is the best reason to look at a residual plot?
c: To check whether a linear model is appropriate
To find the mean of the data
items.e: Patterns in a residual plot show whether a line is the right model.

items.q: Countries with more TVs per person have longer life expectancy. Should a government buy TVs to help people live longer?
c: No, wealth is a likely hidden factor
items.e: Richer countries have both more TVs and better health care. Correlation is not causation.

items.q: The correlation between hours of practice and free-throw percentage is 0.7. Which word describes it?
items.e: 0.7 is positive and fairly close to 1: moderate to strong positive.

items.q: A data point is (5, 30) and the line predicts 34 at x = 5. What is the residual?
items.e: Residual = actual − predicted = 30 − 34 = −4.

items.q: What does it mean if all residuals are positive?
c: The line is too low for every point
The line is too high for every point
items.e: Positive residuals mean every point is above the line: the line is too low; a better line would be higher.

items.q: Which pair of variables would most likely have a negative correlation?
items.e: Older cars are usually worth less: negative.

items.q: A scientist runs a controlled experiment where only one variable is changed. Why can she claim cause and effect?
c: Other factors were kept the same
items.e: In a controlled experiment, other factors are held constant, so changes can be linked to the one variable changed.
